Build a network from the levels of a table

Source: R/visgen.R
df2Network.Rd

Converts a table into the nodes and links tables used by the graph and sankey wrappers (for example visNetwork, grviz, echarts, networkD3 and googleVis). The columns id_cols are consecutive levels of a flow: each value of a level is a node, and a link joins each value of a level to each value of the next level it occurs with, with the sum of value_col over the rows as its value.

Usage

df2Network(df, id_cols = names(df), value_col, percentage = F)

Arguments

df

A data frame.

id_cols

Names of the columns giving the consecutive levels of the network.

value_col

Name of the numeric column summed over the links.

percentage

If TRUE, adds column pathratio to the links: the share (percent) of the flow through the link along the whole path.

Value

A list with two data frames: nodes (columns id and label, like "Class=1st") and links (columns source, target, value, svname, tvname, hovertext, sumval and ratio: the percent of the flow of the source going through the link).

See also

The networks and hierarchies guide.

Examples

titanic <- as.data.frame(Titanic, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
flows <- df2Network(titanic, id_cols = c("Class", "Sex", "Survived"), value_col = "Freq")
head(flows$nodes)
#>           id      label
#> 1 Sex=Female Sex=Female
#> 2   Sex=Male   Sex=Male
#> 3  Class=1st  Class=1st
#> 4  Class=2nd  Class=2nd
#> 5  Class=3rd  Class=3rd
#> 6 Class=Crew Class=Crew
head(flows$links[, c("source", "target", "value", "ratio")])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 4
#> # Groups:   source [3]
#>   source     target       value ratio
#>   <chr>      <chr>        <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1 Sex=Female Survived=No    126  26.8
#> 2 Sex=Female Survived=Yes   344  73.2
#> 3 Sex=Male   Survived=No   1364  78.8
#> 4 Sex=Male   Survived=Yes   367  21.2
#> 5 Class=1st  Sex=Female     145  44.6
#> 6 Class=1st  Sex=Male       180  55.4
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
rvisPlot("sankey", "networkD3", obj = flows, key = "id", label = "label",
         source = "source", target = "target", linkWidth = "value")
} # }
